clue.text: Black-and-white bird without feathers

parts.note: the pie is an old name for the magpie, a crossword staple
a bird with no feathers on its head is bald

explanation.surface: A description of a plucked magpie, black and white with its plumage gone.
explanation.walkthrough: PIEBALD describes a horse patched in black and white; 'bird' gives PIE, the magpie.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald animal has irregular patches of two colours, classically black and white.

clue.text: Beg a top manager to provide cheap fuel

indicators.note: a manager arranges and organises, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking a senior boss to supply inexpensive energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manager' signals rearranging BEG A TOP into PEAT BOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A peat bog supplies peat, cut and dried as a traditional inexpensive fuel.

clue.text: English girl without time for tea? How wearing!

indicators.note: without means outside, so the girl's name goes around the next piece

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
four o'clock is traditional teatime, and IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman too busy to stop for a cuppa exclaims at how tiring it all is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; four o'clock is the traditional British teatime, so IV. 'How' is a link to the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosive means wearing away gradually, as water erodes rock.

clue.text: A look of disdain, clearly

parts.note: describes a distant, standoffish expression, with 'clearly' nodding that the letters nearly show in the opening words

explanation.surface: Someone's face plainly shows contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means cool and distant, the bearing of someone who holds others in disdain.

clue.text: Admit Len's about to do demolition work

indicators.note: about means around and astir, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Confessing that Len is going to knock something down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ADMIT LENS into DISMANTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to take a structure apart piece by piece, a kind of demolition.

clue.text: Survive when dismissed after everyone else

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
coming after all others means being last

explanation.surface: A cricketer who survives longest is the one dismissed after all the others.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who is dismissed is OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast someone is to live or endure longer than they do, so to survive them.

clue.text: Harangue makes men fed up

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers
having fed means one ate

explanation.surface: A rant that leaves the troops thoroughly sick of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' reads as weary, but it is ATE; OR is 'other ranks', the non-officers.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a pompous speech, and harangue is a verb for lecturing at length.

clue.text: Seaman appears in suit for a change

indicators.note: the sailor is placed inside the outfit word

parts.note: a turnout is a person's outfit or get-up
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor turns up in a new suit for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears in' is the container signal; a turnout is an old word for someone's outfit or get-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnabout is a reversal of direction or opinion, a complete switch.

clue.text: Excited when offered employment in a bar

indicators.note: in places the employment word inside the bar word

parts.note: a rod is a metal bar
use means employment, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to land a job working behind a pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but means a metal rod; 'in' is the container signal, and 'when offered' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Aroused means stirred up or stimulated, the same as excited.

clue.text: Quality gold given to Judas

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic quality
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Fine gold handed to Judas, echoing his thirty pieces of silver.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name stands for any betrayer.

clue.text: A doctor's got our backing for being passionate

indicators.note: has got around, so the doctor's letters hold the next piece

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor; the 's adds S

indicators.note: backing means read the word our from back to front

parts.note: taken as the word itself, reversed

explanation.surface: A doctor whose ardent manner has won the patients' support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' (has got, holds) is the container signal and 'backing' the reversal; strictly the reversed word comes out in a different order from what the grid needs, so the clue is slightly off.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means full of romantic or sexual desire, a strongly passionate state.

clue.text: A small headlight

parts.note: not a lamp on a car but a little ring of light round someone's head, as in a saint's halo

explanation.surface: Apparently a modest lamp on the front of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An aureola is a radiant circle or halo of light painted around a holy figure's head.

clue.text: Barrister takes suit in paper-carrier

parts.note: a barrister's instructions are the brief, and 'brief' is slang for a lawyer
a lawsuit is a legal case

explanation.surface: A barrister taking on a lawsuit carries the papers in his bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat bag for carrying documents.

clue.text: Hardy girl with a retrospective advantage

indicators.note: looking back, so the girl's name and the letter are read backwards

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A Hardy heroine looking back over a past benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns TESS + A into ASSET; Tess is the title heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable quality, a benefit.

clue.text: Ideal horses for cavalry regiment

parts.note: reads as advice on mounts, but points to a famous regiment named after the colour of its horses

explanation.surface: Recommended mounts for a mounted army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Scots Greys were a British cavalry regiment, named for their grey horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Greys are grey-coated horses, and the Scots Greys were the regiment that rode them.

clue.text: The cantos composed by a songster

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: Poetic cantos written by a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges THE CANTOS into STONECHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small songbird named for its call, like stones knocking together.

clue.text: Dire task for brotherhood of high standing

parts.note: standing high means being tall
a religious or knightly brotherhood is an order

explanation.surface: A hard job assigned to an exalted fraternity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a demand that is very difficult to fulfil.

clue.text: Tall man's underclothing

parts.note: tall means long
John is a man's name; the 's gives S

explanation.surface: A lanky fellow's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Long johns are warm full-length underpants.

clue.text: Whole lane involved in October festival

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the two words are mixed

explanation.surface: An entire street taking part in an autumn celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges WHOLE and LANE into HALLOWEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween falls on 31 October, the eve of All Saints' Day.

clue.text: Henry and mohammad have objection to fish

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Muhammad Ali, the boxer
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Two men raising a complaint about a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ali gives ALI.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish of northern seas.

clue.text: Obvious place to buy Swiss fodder

definitions.text: Obvious place to buy Swiss fodder

parts.words: Obvious place to buy Swiss fodder
parts.note: a Swiss city shares its name with a forage crop, so it is the natural market for it

explanation.surface: Where you would naturally shop for animal feed in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The crop also called alfalfa, grown for fodder, shares its name with the Swiss city.

clue.text: Heard brief monastic service

indicators.note: what is heard is a word spoken, so the synonym for brief is taken by its sound

parts.note: brief and curt mean terse

explanation.surface: Someone listened to a short religious office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' signals that TERSE (brief) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Terce is the canonical hour of prayer said at the third hour of the day.

clue.text: Rebel leader gets backing after mounting attacks

indicators.note: the leader of the rebel is the word's first letter

parts.note: backing someone means supporting or helping them, so aiding

explanation.surface: A rebel chief gains support and then launches assaults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' means helping, AIDING, put after R, the first letter of 'Rebel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiding means carrying out surprise attacks.

clue.text: A factor in the weather?

parts.note: a component of something, and also one of the forces of nature we brave outdoors

explanation.surface: Asking what contributes to the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component, and the elements are wind, rain and the weather.

clue.text: Many beset by temptation to make money

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the temptation word encloses the number

parts.note: a lure is an enticement or temptation
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

explanation.surface: A great number of people giving in to the urge to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' puts C (Roman 100, 'many') inside LURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, usually in the disapproving phrase filthy lucre.

clue.text: Aim to be unprejudiced

definitions.meaning: free from bias or personal feeling

explanation.surface: Striving to be fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a goal; as an adjective it means impartial and fact-based.

clue.text: Veteran soldier takes it to heart

indicators.note: the heart of soldier is everything inside its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An old soldier who is deeply affected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes it to heart' means use the inner letters of 'soldier'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old person or thing, someone long in service.

clue.text: Initially eastern actors had social status

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of eastern

explanation.surface: Early oriental performers enjoyed social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives E from 'eastern', placed after CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Caste is a hereditary social class, especially in Hindu society.

clue.text: Given sleeping accommodation in dock

definitions.meaning: provided with a bunk on a ship or train

explanation.surface: A traveller shown to a bunk while the ship is moored.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is both a bunk to sleep in and a ship's mooring place, so the verb covers both senses.

clue.text: New hotel is very unfriendly

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A recently opened hotel that gives guests a cold welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges HOTEL IS into HOSTILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile means openly antagonistic, much stronger than merely cool.

clue.text: Ops room

parts.note: sounds like a military operations room, but refers to the room where surgical operations are done

explanation.surface: A military command centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is the hospital room where surgery is performed.

clue.text: Stratagem used by small, level-headed crew

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the head, or first letter, of level is L
a rowing eight is the crew of an eight-oared boat

explanation.surface: A clever plan devised by a little, calm-minded team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'level-headed' is read as the head of 'level', giving L, not as calm; an eight is a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means cunning or a crafty trick, as in sleight of hand.
